destinations
Discover Türkiye’s inspiring towns and villages that embrace local culture, live in harmony with nature, and offer authentic experiences to visitors. Internationally recognized,
these special destinations connect the past with the future through a strong commitment to sustainability.
Halfeti
Halfeti is in the westernmost part of the province of Şanlıurfa and on the east bank of the Euphrates River. With a 3,000-year-old history, Halfeti is one of Türkiye's most extraordinary locations.
Güdül
One of the smallest districts of Ankara Province, Güdül is about 90 km from the center of Ankara. Excavations in and around the city have exposed the region’s long history.
Göynük
Göynük, an urban site that has preserved its historical, cultural, architectural and natural beauties from the Ottomans to the present, holds the title of a Slow Town (Cittaslow).
Gökçeada
It is located in the northwest Aegean region, and is Türkiye’s largest island. It is famous for its singular geography and protected natural resources.
Foça
The district of Foça is situated on the site of the ancient city of Phocaea and is said to have been founded by the very same people who founded the French city of Marseilles, Attalia in Corsica and Ampurias in Catalonia.
Eğirdir
Situated in Isparta Province and around, Eğirdir is one of Türkiye’s 21 members of Cittaslow International.
Arapgir
In 2021, the Arapgir district was designated as a Cittaslow (Slow City). It is also the first district of Malatya to be granted ‘The Cittaslow Status’.
Akyaka
Imagine a quiet town located between the lush mountains and the turquoise sea.
Ahlat
Ahlat, a historical city in the district of Bitlis, northwest of Lake Van, welcomes visitors with an arresting sight of glorious tombstones dating back to the Seljuk period.
Taraklı
A small town to the southwest of Sakarya, Taraklı, with its graceful wooden houses and narrow streets, has masterfully protected its Ottoman atmosphere and slow yet vibrant lifestyle.
Mustafapaşa
Mustafapaşa, formerly known as Sinasos, is a small town with 1,300 inhabitants and stone buildings set along the feet of five surrounding hills.
Kemaliye
The Historic Town of Kemaliye, entered on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List in 2021, features traditional houses that draw attention due to their architecture.
Köyceğiz
At the easternmost part of the Mediterranean, the southernmost part of the Aegean Sea, at the junction of the Carian and Lycian civilizations, there is a region where blue and green dance together and where history is as ancient as time itself.
Bursa
Just sit for a moment and think about all the beautiful things once you’ve seen and adored. Nature, history, fun, art…
Kırşehir
The Land of Minstrels, the City of Ahiler… Kırşehir is an ancient city where astronomers have trained for millennia, witnessed by 4000 years of history...
Afyonkarahisar
Afyonkarahisar is a part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network with its rich gastronomy heritage.
Kütahya
As an ancient place in Anatolian geography, Kütahya’s history dates from prehistoric times (stone age-mine age).
Hatay
Hatay is a part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network with its rich gastronomy heritage.
Gaziantep
Gaziantep is a part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network with its rich gastronomy heritage.
Yenipazar
Yenipazar is a small and quiet district located in western Türkiye, in the Aegean region. It is 40 km from Aydın city center, and 100 kilometers from Kuşadası.
Vize
Vize, a town and district in Kırklareli Province on Türkiye's European soil, is located between two former Ottoman capitals: İstanbul and Edirne.
Uzundere
Uzundere, a town and district of Erzurum Province, is located on the borders of the Black Sea region and the region of Eastern Anatolia.
Seferihisar
Situated in the south of İzmir city, Seferihisar is the meeting point of nature, history, and the sea. It is the first town in Türkiye to join the Cittaslow movement.
Şavşat
Situated in the eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye, known for its eternal green scenery and clean air...
Perşembe
The altitude of the plateau in Aybastı district is around 1500 meters.
Mudurnu
Located between İstanbul and Ankara, Mudurnu is a small town and district in the province of Bolu.
İznik
İznik (ancient Nicaea) is a beautiful town on the lakeside offering rich natural and historical attractions.
Ejder 3200
Türkiye’s one of the most popular skiing destinations, Ejder 3200 (Palandöken Ski Center) is now certified by the Global Sustainable Tourism Council (GSTC) as a sustainable destination!
Çameli
Afyonkarahisar is a part of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network with its rich gastronomy heritage.

10 Must-See Excavation Sites in Türkiye
Türkiye has a richly diverse and many layered history. With archaeological sites dating back to neolithic times like Gobeklitepe, mythical cities like Hattusa whose secrets are still being discovered and famous ancient cities like Ephesus, Pergamon and Troy; Türkiye is waiting for you to come and uncover the mysteries of its past. Whether you’re interested in casually exploring ruins by boat, like the sunken city of Kekova on the Mediterranean or Olympos further along the coast. Or a keen explorer, intent on learning as much as possible about the ancients of Catalhoyuk, Türkiye and her ancient tales are waiting for you.
